unitemized.reason: Frontend accessibility standard about heading levels in UI markup. It applies only if the change touches frontend views, and there is no predicate for that condition. Judging the order of headings in produced HTML is beyond any kind.
Style preference for CSS units. It applies only to UI styling changes and needs a subjective code review; no predicate or kind expresses it.
Testing UI across multiple screen sizes only applies to UI changes (condition not expressible). Device-size testing leaves no recognisable test-run evidence.
Tap-target sizing is a UI design property of rendered components. It cannot be checked from the trace or diff with the available kinds, and it applies only to UI changes.
Keeping code style consistent is a subjective judgment on code quality; no kind expresses it.
Whether a name is meaningful, and the 'narrow contexts' exception, is a subjective judgment on code quality; no kind expresses it.
Consistent indentation is a code style property that no available kind checks.
Configuring an editor or linter is project-setup advice from a general standards file. It is not a requirement on this run's actions or artifacts, and no observable condition ties it to the run.
Preferring specific exception types is a subjective design guideline for code; no kind expresses it.
